newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Australia, Mauritius study fertiliser use on sugar.
newsitem.headline: Australia, Mauritius study fertiliser use on sugar.

text.p: Australia and a research institute in Mauritius agreed on Tuesday to study the potential environmental threat of fertilisers and other chemicals applied to sugar cane.

Australia's Queensland Department of Natural Resources (QDNR) and the Mauritius Sugar Industry Reseach Institute (MSIRI) signed a memorandum of understanding for the study. fertilisers and other agrochemical products, officials said.
The study, supported by the Canberra-based Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research, will last three-and-a-half years and cost A$2.9 million.

"It should be emphasised that this is the first major study on the fate and risks of agrochemicals applied to sugar cane across the world and that given the aspects encompassed into it, the results will keep MSIRI and QDNR in the forefront in this field of research," said MSIRI Director Jean Claude Autrey.
Sixteen MSIRI and 29 QDNR scientists will be involved in the project in Mauritius, which was chosen as the research site because of its range of micro-climates, topography and humid tropical weather.
Mauritius applies some 60,000 tonnes of fertilisers and 11,000 tonnes of herbicides to 77,000 hectares of sugar cane annually and without adverse weather can produce about 650,000 tonnes of sugar.
